free_tier.stated: None: the API endpoint answers <error code="101" description="This API endpoint has been retired. Update your indexer URL from nzb.su to nzb.life."/> The name still resolves, the indexer behind it has moved.

retention.stated: not applicable under this name; the successor publishes its own caps

egress.terms: none: the endpoint returns a 157-byte error document

record.interface_detail: The /api path is alive and answers XML, but only with error 101. This is the cleanest death signal in the sector: a machine-readable redirect to the successor, not a timeout.
record.tooling: A Prowlarr or NZBHydra2 entry pointed at nzb.su keeps the URL and receives error 101 on every search; the fix is to change the host to nzb.life, not to re-add the indexer.
record.chaining: Retired in favour of nzb.life, which carries the live limits.

limits.value: the indexer URL is retired; every API call returns error 101

record.binding_note: The name is the constraint: no query reaches an index. The successor record carries the live limits.

identity_cost.detail: Accounts and registration were carried to nzb.life; the old host no longer offers a path.

record.reliability_note: A retired API with a live DNS record: a stale client gets a well-formed XML error, which most clients log as an empty result set rather than as a configuration problem.
record.confidence_note: The error document was fetched with its exact wording, so the retirement is measured. The successor's limits are on the nzb-life record.

evidence.proved: returned 157 bytes: <error code="101" description="This API endpoint has been retired. Update your indexer URL from nzb.su to nzb.life."/> (sha256 867011a3...)
the successor states the mapping in its own meta description: 'NZB.su and nzbsu users should use NZB.life.'

record.notes: Do not delete: the old host is still in circulating lists and in old client configs, and the error message is the only thing that tells a reader where the index went.
